newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS ANOTHER TITLE BUT HINGIS STEALS SHOW.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS ANOTHER TITLE BUT HINGIS STEALS SHOW.

text.p: Pete Sampras fought like a champion to clinch the toughest of his nine Grand Slam titles but the star of the show at the Australian Open was a Swiss teenager who breezed to her first major title.
Confident, cheeky, supremely gifted, 16-year-old Martina Hingis made every game look easy as she stormed through the women's draw to become the youngest Grand Slam champion ever.
True, she never had to meet Steffi Graf, Germany's troubled world number one who made a fourth-round exit, or defending champion Monica Seles, who was nursing a broken finger.
Yet Hingis's performance in Melbourne suggested both might have met the same fate as former champion Mary Pierce, beaten in under an hour in Saturday's women's final.

Hingis takes the ball early, hits it impossibly hard for a girl so slight and anticipates her opponents' moves like a veteran. No-one questioned her when she said that only injury could come between her and Graf's number one spot.

The year's first Grand Slam had its problems: Sampras and others complained the balls were too heavy, women players complained about playing in a heatwave and everyone complained when the referee closed the Centre Court roof to shut out the sun.
"It was like playing in an oven," said unseeded Belgian Dominique van Roost, who beat number two seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain in the third round.
"You cannot try (for) the whole game otherwise you die -- after 10 minutes you're dead," added Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic.
The heat was partly to blame for the most spectacular day of the tournament, when four top women including Graf exited.

Graf stayed in Melbourne after her defeat, receiving treatment for heat exhaustion and an infected toe while waiting for a German court to sentence her father for tax evasion on millions of dollars of her earnings.
But the least prestigious of the four major tournaments of tennis witnessed some heroic performances.
After beating Sanchez Vicario, Van Roost ignored a back injury to beat 15th-seeded Chanda Rubin of the United States. A pulled abdominal muscle ended her campaign in the next match.
Twelfth seed Amanda Coetzer, who beat Graf, produced some storming tennis to beat American Kimberly Po in the quarter-finals, only to be swept aside by Pierce in the semifinals.

Only one player in the Open era of tennis, Sweden's Bjorn Borg with 11, has more Grand Slam titles to his name than Sampras. All-time Grand Slam leaders include Australians Roy Emerson and Rod Laver, with 12 and 11 respectively, and the American 1920s great Bill Tilden, who won 10 majors.
Sampras, 25, did it the hard way, surviving two five-setters on his way to the final for what he called the toughest major title of his career.
"I've never played in conditions like that, ever," said Sampras of the Melbourne heat.

One of those who took him the distance was Grand Slam debutant Dominik Hrbaty, a 19-year-old from Slovakia who turned professional only last year. Sampras said before the match he did not know what the Slovak looked like, although he gave the young Hrbaty an autograph in Paris three years ago.
"Maybe next time he ask me for autograph," said the Slovak, only half-joking.

The other player to take Sampras to five sets was 10th-seeded Spaniard Albert Costa. Sampras must have had a touch of deja vu after his exhausting four-hour battle with another Spaniard, Alex Corretja, at last year's U.S. Open.
But the next member of Spain's Melbourne Armada forgot to bring his weapons. The final against unseeded Carlos Moya turned out to be a disappointingly one-sided affair.
Moya caused two of the Open's biggest upsets when he beat defending champion Boris Becker in the first round and world number two Michael Chang in the semifinals.
But Sampras, who said he felt his late coach Tim Gullikson was looking down on him, served 12 aces and dominated from both net and baseline to beat Moya 6-2 6-3 6-3 in one hour 27 minutes.
"He's number one and he showed it today," said the 20-year-old Barcelona baseliner. "It's better to meet him in the first or second round, not in the final. In the final, he's almost unbeatable."
